info.description:
Welcome to the **Happily.ai API**, the fastest way to plug recognition,
engagement surveys, performance feedback, and people analytics into your
own products and workflows.

Use it to sync your employee directory from an HRIS, send recognition from a
Slack bot, run performance review cycles programmatically, or pull survey
responses into your data warehouse.

> [!NOTE]
> **New to the API?** Start with the [Quickstart](/guides/quickstart.html) —
> you'll make your first authenticated call in under five minutes.

## Base URL

All requests are made over HTTPS to a stage-scoped base URL on the
`api.happily.ai` custom domain:

```
https://api.happily.ai/{stage}
```

| `{stage}` | Use for                 |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `prod`    | Live company data.      |
| `staging` | Pre-production testing. |
| `dev`     | Development / sandbox.  |

Your API key is bound to a single stage. Each endpoint path carries its own
version prefix: most endpoints live under `/1/...`, and newer ones (member
import, performance boosts and presets, user profiles) live under
`/api/v1/...`. A full request URL therefore looks like
`https://api.happily.ai/prod/1/recognition` or
`https://api.happily.ai/prod/api/v1/users/{email}/profile`.

> [!NOTE]
> Paths below are confirmed against the deployed API Gateway (`ln1buvf68h`,
> region `us-east-2`). A few newer endpoints are marked "⚠" where the exact
> path is still being finalized. See the
> [Migration guide](/guides/migration.html) for what changed from the old docs.

## Authentication

Every request must include your secret API key in the **`x-api-key`** header.
Keys are issued per company and per stage. Generate or rotate keys at
[my.happily.ai/integrations](https://my.happily.ai/integrations).

```bash
curl https://api.happily.ai/prod/1/members?email=jordan@acme.com \
  -H "x-api-key: $HAPPILY_API_KEY"
```

Treat your key like a password — it grants full access to your company's
data. Never commit it or expose it in client-side code. See the
[Authentication guide](/guides/authentication.html).

## Rate limits

Write-heavy endpoints (currently **member import**) are limited to
**10 requests per minute, per API key**. When you exceed the limit the API
responds with a `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` error and a `reset_at` timestamp telling
you when the window clears. Successful import responses also echo a
`rate_limit` object with your remaining quota. See
[Rate limits](/guides/rate-limits.html).

## Pagination

List endpoints accept `page` (1-based) and `limit` (default `50`, max `250`)
query parameters and return a `pagination` object:

```json
{
  "pagination": {
    "currentPage": 1,
    "totalPages": 4,
    "totalItems": 183,
    "pageSize": 50
  }
}
```

See [Pagination](/guides/pagination.html).

## Responses & errors

Responses are JSON. Successful responses carry the resource fields plus a
`statusCode` and, for collections, a named array (e.g. `members`,
`recognitions`) and a `pagination` object. Errors carry a `statusCode`, an
`error: true` flag, a human-readable message, and (for most endpoints) a
machine-readable `error_code`:

```json
{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "error": true,
  "errorMsg": "email and question_id are required",
  "error_code": "VALIDATION_ERROR"
}
```

The full list of error codes lives in the [Errors guide](/guides/errors.html).

Resolve a medal/reward identifier to its configured value for your
company. If the medal is not configured, the `value` echoes the

post.description:
Give recognition (coins) on behalf of `member_email`. Recipients can be
one or more individuals, an entire team or cohort, or **all members**.

**`recipients`** accepts several shapes:

| Form                 | Example                                  |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Single email         | `"jordan@acme.com"`                       |
| Comma-separated list | `"jordan@acme.com,sam@acme.com"`          |
| Array of emails      | `["jordan@acme.com", "sam@acme.com"]`     |
| Everyone             | `"ALL_MEMBERS"`                           |
| Team / cohort IDs    | `"t123456789"` (team) · `"c123456789"` (cohort) |

Unknown individual recipients cause a `503` error; unknown teams/cohorts
are skipped. The sender (`member_email`) must belong to your company.

> Path confirmed against API Gateway (`dev` · `prod` · `staging`).

post.description:
Bulk-create or update members, typically synced from an HRIS. Submit up
to **1,000 members** per request. Each member is validated; the import
succeeds only if **every** member is valid (unless duplicates are handled
via `options`).

**Duplicate handling** (`options`):
- `skip_duplicates: true` — silently skip members whose email already exists.
- `update_if_exists: true` — update existing members instead of failing.
- Neither set — a duplicate email fails validation.

This endpoint is **rate limited to 10 requests/minute per API key**. The
response echoes your remaining quota in `rate_limit`. Imports are queued
for asynchronous processing and tracked by the returned `import_id`.

> ⚠ Inferred path. The gateway exposes `/api/v1/members`; the import is
> the `POST` on that resource. Confirm the method before publishing.

sync.summary: Sync two members, updating any that already exist

400.description: Validation failed — one or more members are invalid.

post.description:
Submit one or more performance review "boosts". Send a single object or
an array (max **200** per request). Each boost is validated and processed
independently — the response is an array of per-item results, each either
a success or an error.

**Rules per boost:**
- The `reviewer_email` must be the **direct manager** of `employee_email`.
- Both people must belong to your company.
- `supporting_examples` is required for both goal and culture sections.
- A member can't be reviewed again until their review cycle resets.

> ⚠ Inferred path. The gateway exposes both `/1/performance-boosts` and
> `/api/v1/performance-boosts`; this documents the `/api/v1` form.
> Confirm which is canonical before publishing.

future_development.goals_targets_outcomes: Lead the mobile redesign next quarter.

goal_performance.supporting_examples: Hit all three OKRs and unblocked the launch.

200.description: Per-item results (some items may have failed).

existing presets so each is assigned to only one preset.
